# Sorted grid and table headers do not announce their sort direction

**Claim it first:** comment on this issue before you start, and check the open pull requests for one that already points here. We merge the first approve-worthy PR (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`, point 3).

## Context

Welcome! A small accessibility fix in Neo.mjs's grid and table headers. You need a fork, Node and the dev server; no Agent OS, Docker or AI tooling.

A column header is a `<button role="columnheader">`. When you sort a column, the header shows an arrow, but a screen reader is not told: nothing sets [`aria-sort`](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-sort), the attribute that announces "sorted ascending" or "sorted descending". A search for `aria-sort` in `src/` finds nothing.

## The Problem

To see it:

1. `npm install`, then `npm run server-start`.
2. Open `http://localhost:8080/examples/grid/issues/index.html`. The `#` column starts sorted.
3. Inspect its header in DevTools: `<button role="columnheader" … class="… neo-sort-desc …">`, with a class for the arrow and no `aria-sort`.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/grid/header/Button.mjs` `afterSetIsSorted(value)` turns the sort state into CSS classes: `null` adds `neo-sort-hidden`, `'ASC'` sets `neo-sort-asc`, `'DESC'` sets `neo-sort-desc`. It is the one place that already reacts to every sort change.
- `removeSortingCss()` in the same file clears a header's sort by resetting `_isSorted` directly, so it bypasses `afterSetIsSorted()` and needs its own update.
- `src/table/header/Button.mjs` has the same two methods.
- `test/playwright/unit/grid/HeaderButtonSortable.spec.mjs` already drives both buttons; unit tests run locally.

## The Fix

In both header buttons, set `aria-sort` alongside the classes: `ascending` for `'ASC'`, `descending` for `'DESC'`, and no `aria-sort` for an unsorted header (per WAI-ARIA, only the sorted header carries it). Clear it in `removeSortingCss()` as well. Add unit cases to `HeaderButtonSortable.spec.mjs` for both buttons.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A grid header sorted ascending carries `aria-sort="ascending"`, sorted descending `aria-sort="descending"`, and an unsorted header carries none, including after `removeSortingCss()`.
- [ ] AC-2 The table header button behaves the same.
- [ ] AC-3 `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/grid/HeaderButtonSortable.spec.mjs` passes and covers all three states for both buttons.

## Out of Scope

- The header menus' own option labels (#19878).
- Announcing multi-column sort order.

### @sunred-liu - 2026-10-20T11:33:45Z

I'll take this one.

Plan matches the "The Fix" section: `aria-sort` on the columnheader in both header buttons, cleared in
`removeSortingCss()` too, plus the three cases per button in `HeaderButtonSortable.spec.mjs`.

One detail worth flagging before I open the PR: in the grid the button *is* the `columnheader`, so the attribute
goes where `changeVdomRootKey()` already writes `role`. In the table the columnheader is the `<th>`, and
`getVdomRoot()` deliberately points one level down at the native button (top-level style attributes belong there),
so I write `aria-sort` to `this.vdom` there. Putting it on a `role=button` would be invalid per WAI-ARIA 1.2 and
would announce nothing. Say the word if you'd rather have it on the button in both for consistency.
